verdict: INFER NETWORK (infer_network.py): built the cell's wiring FROM the knockout data instead of testing databases against it. Each row is an intervention, so |z[A,B]| past a calibrated threshold is a directed, signed, MEASURED causal edge. BUILD: of 1971 knockouts only 337 (17%) move >=20 genes and can carry an edge at all; those yield 21,228 measured directed edges. PATTERN: the network is extremely asymmetric -- the top 10% of sources carry 32% of all edges, and of the 2,610 edges whose target is itself a usable knockout only 5.4% are mirrored back, so measured causation is one-way, not mutual. THE HEADLINE: 94.0% of these measured causal edges appear in NO curated layer we hold (and this is NOT a tide artifact -- restricting to the 8,726 knockout-SPECIFIC edges makes it 98.0% novel, worse than the tide edges' 91.2%) (regulatory 0.07%, PPI 5.94%, complex 1.36%) -- the databases and the measured causal graph are almost disjoint objects, which is why every annotation-first attempt in this project stalled. VERIFY: on a random sample, cross-cell-line reproduction where testable runs 32%, giving a graded confidence (curated support / reciprocity / cross-line) rather than a binary edge. DRAW IT WITHOUT PERTURB-SEQ: against DEGREE-MATCHED negatives, non-perturbation features reach AUC 0.542 (best single: DepMap co-dependency 0.506). That is only modestly above chance, so static annotation and co-dependency can rank candidate edges but cannot reconstruct the causal graph on their own -- consistent with the near-disjointness above. MEANING: the measured knockout graph is a different object from the curated interactome, mostly one-way, hub-dominated, and largely absent from databases. That is the map worth building; the open question is how cheaply it can be drafted from static features and how much must be measured. Deterministic; degree-matched controls throughout.
